result: Conditional knockout of Ttbk2 in adult mice (Ttbk2c.mut) results in motor coordination deficits as measured by rotarod performance tests.
evaluation: Claims C6, C35, C36, and C37 collectively demonstrate that Ttbk2c.mut mice exhibit significantly shorter latency to fall on both accelerating and steady speed rotarod tests (Figure 1A,B), with appropriate statistical analysis (p<0.0001 and p=0.0001, n=8-9 animals). The behavioral phenotype is consistent with motor deficits in other SCA mouse models.

result: Loss of TTBK2 in adult mice causes reduction in VGLUT2+ climbing fiber synapses and thinning of the cerebellar molecular layer.
evaluation: Claims C38-C40, C51-C52 are supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data showing significant reduction in VGLUT2 puncta (527.3±12.68 vs 297.8±15.65, p<0.0001) and molecular layer thickness (175±3.4 vs 160.9±2.5 μm, p=0.0011) in Ttbk2c.mut animals at 3 months post-TMX (Figure 1C-E). Statistical tests are appropriate with n=3 animals.

result: The loss of VGLUT2 synapses in Ttbk2c.mut animals occurs without loss of dendritic spines or gross morphological changes to Purkinje cell dendritic arbors.
evaluation: Claims C41, C53, and C56 are supported by Golgi staining data showing no significant difference in spine density (1.236±0.22 vs 1.368±0.32 spines/μm) and imaging showing intact dendritic arbors (Figure 1F,G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B). This indicates synaptic loss is not due to structural dendritic degeneration.

result: IP3R expression is reduced in Purkinje cells of Ttbk2c.mut animals starting at P45 and is strongly reduced by 3 months post-TMX.
evaluation: Claims C42, C43, and C48 are supported by immunostaining data showing progressive loss of IP3R expression in PCs (Figure 1H). The temporal progression from P45 to 3 months is documented, though quantification is not provided. This is consistent with calcium signaling dysfunction in other SCA models (C46-C47).

result: Loss of TTBK2 after cerebellar development is complete (P45 injection) leads to degeneration of VGLUT2+ synapses.
evaluation: Claims C54 and C55 are supported by experimental data showing that Ttbk2c.mut animals injected at P45 exhibit the same loss of VGLUT2+ synapses (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-B, p<0.0001). This demonstrates the phenotype is not due to developmental defects but rather maintenance requirements in the adult cerebellum.

result: Neurons in the inferior olivary nucleus (ION) show reduced soma area in Ttbk2c.mut animals.
evaluation: Claims C57 and C58 are supported by quantitative NeuN immunostaining showing significant reduction in ION neuron soma area (180.4±1.93 vs 109±1.01 μm², p<0.0001, >150 cells measured per animal, n=3) (Figure 2A,B). This neuronal shrinkage is consistent with phenotypes in other SCA models (C59-C60).

result: Bergmann glia fiber density is moderately reduced in Ttbk2c.mut animals.
evaluation: Claims C61 and C62 are supported by GFAP immunostaining showing significant reduction in BG fiber density (11.44±0.29 vs 7.64±0.22 fibers, p<0.0001, 36 images per genotype, n=3) (Figure 2C,D). The effect is described as modest, suggesting non-cell-autonomous effects on glia.

result: At P30, Ttbk2Pcp2 animals (PC-specific knockout) have normal cerebellar structure and VGLUT2+ synapses.
evaluation: Claims C64-C66 are supported by quantitative data showing no significant differences in molecular layer thickness (202.7±3.51 vs 191.5±3.21 μm) or VGLUT2 puncta (548.2±13.36 vs 538.9±18.14) at P30 (Figure 3A,C,D). This demonstrates that initial synaptic connections form normally despite postnatal loss of Ttbk2.

result: By P90, Ttbk2Pcp2 animals exhibit loss of cilia on PCs and reduction in VGLUT2+ synapses without changes in molecular layer thickness.
evaluation: Claims C67-C71 are supported by data showing significant reduction in ciliated PCs (48.93±7.86% vs 18.67±11.07%, p<0.0001) and VGLUT2 puncta (549.9±15.47 vs 476.9±15.82, p=0.0098) at P90, while molecular layer thickness remains unchanged (Figure 3B-D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1). This demonstrates progressive synaptic degeneration.

result: Ttbk2Pcp2 animals develop motor coordination deficits by P90 but not at P30.
evaluation: Claims C72 and C73 are supported by rotarod data showing no significant deficits at P30 (p=0.1051 accelerating, p=0.7819 steady speed) but significant deficits at P90 (p=0.0161 accelerating, p=0.0023 steady speed) (Figure 3E,F, n=4-6 animals). This temporal progression correlates with synaptic loss.

result: Loss of Ttbk2 specifically from Purkinje cells causes neurodegenerative phenotypes in a cell-autonomous manner.
evaluation: Claims C74-C76 are supported by comparing Pcp2-Cre (PC-specific) and Slc1a3-CreER (glia-specific) knockouts. PC-specific knockout recapitulates the phenotype (C67-C73), while glia-specific knockout shows no changes in VGLUT2 synapses (Figure 3G-I). This demonstrates cell autonomy of the PC phenotype.

result: At 6 months of age, Ttbk2c.mut mice show progressive loss of Purkinje cells with gaps in the molecular layer, particularly in inner folia but not folia X.
evaluation: Claims C77-C80 are supported by quantitative data showing significant PC loss at 6 months (18.67±0.43 vs 11.92±0.74 PCs per 500 μm, p<0.0001) but not at 4 months (Figure 4A,B). Gap distribution analysis shows enrichment in inner folia (I-IX) but not folia X (Figure 4C), consistent with known resistance of folia X to neurodegeneration (C80, Tolbert et al., 1995).

result: Mild accumulation of phosphorylated Tau is observed in cortical neurons of 6-month-old but not 4-month-old Ttbk2c.mut animals.
evaluation: Claims C82-C84 are supported by AT8 immunostaining showing no phosphorylated Tau in 4-month-old animals but mild accumulation in some cortical neurons at 6 months (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A). This recapitulates SCA11 patient pathology (C81, Houlden et al., 2007), though the accumulation is modest compared to JNPL3 controls.

result: Ttbk2c.mut mice rapidly lose cilia throughout the brain within 20 days of TMX administration, preceding cellular changes but coinciding with behavioral deficits.
evaluation: Claims C85-C88 are supported by quantitative data showing dramatic reduction in ciliated cells (22.46±0.76 vs 2.36±0.31 cilia per 32 mm² field, p<0.0001) within 20 days post-TMX throughout cerebellum, brainstem, hippocampus, and cortex (Figure 5D,E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The temporal relationship establishes cilia loss precedes cellular degeneration but coincides with motor deficits.

result: Ift88c.mut animals show partial loss of cilia with reduced length at 3 months post-TMX, with some IFT88 protein perduring in brain tissue.
evaluation: Claims C94-C96 are supported by quantitative data showing moderate reduction in cilia number (17.31±0.65 vs 12.13±0.50 per 32 mm² field, p<0.0001) and length (2.31±0.10 vs 1.70±0.08 μm, p<0.0001) (Figure 6A,C,D). Western blot confirms residual IFT88 protein (Figure 6B), explaining why cilia loss is less complete than in Ttbk2c.mut.

result: Ift88c.mut animals show strong reduction in AC3+ cilia, suggesting IFT88 is required for localization of specific signaling molecules to neuronal cilia.
evaluation: Claims C97-C99 are supported by quantitative immunofluorescence showing significant reduction in AC3+ cilia (7.47±0.41 vs 2.17±0.22 per 32 mm² field, p<0.0001) despite persistence of ARL13B+ cilia (Figure 6E-G). This demonstrates IFT88 is required for proper ciliary protein localization, particularly AC3, a key cAMP-producing enzyme.

result: Ift88c.mut animals exhibit cerebellar phenotypes similar to Ttbk2c.mut, including reduced molecular layer thickness, VGLUT2 puncta loss, and motor coordination deficits on steady speed rotarod.
evaluation: Claims C100-C104 and C106 are supported by quantitative data showing reduced molecular layer thickness (182.3±2.5 vs 169.3±3.04 μm, p=0.0037), VGLUT2 puncta (515.7±20.58 vs 395.6±13.7, p<0.0001), and steady speed rotarod deficits (p=0.0005) but not accelerating rotarod deficits (p=0.8343) at 3 months (Figure 7). The convergence of phenotypes supports ciliary dysfunction as the mechanism.

result: At 6 months, Ift88c.mut animals show progressive PC loss, further reduction in molecular layer thickness, and diminished VGLUT2 puncta.
evaluation: Claims C107-C110 are supported by quantitative data showing significant PC loss at 6 months (17.17±0.55 vs 12.67±0.43 per 500 μm, p<0.0001), reduced molecular layer thickness (173.9±2.28 vs 158.0±1.63 μm, p<0.0001), and VGLUT2 puncta (645.9±26.83 vs 461.4±25.42, p<0.0001) (Figure 8). This demonstrates progressive neurodegeneration similar to Ttbk2c.mut.

result: The convergence of cerebellar phenotypes between Ttbk2c.mut and Ift88c.mut mice indicates that disruption of ciliary signaling is the primary driver of neurodegeneration.
evaluation: Claims C9, C10, C111, and C127 are supported by the high degree of phenotypic overlap between Ttbk2c.mut and Ift88c.mut animals across multiple measures (motor deficits, synaptic loss, molecular layer thinning, PC loss) despite different mechanisms of ciliary dysfunction (complete vs partial cilia loss with altered protein localization). This convergence strongly supports ciliary dysfunction as the causal mechanism.

result: Primary cilia play a critical role in maintaining Purkinje cell function and connectivity in the adult cerebellum, and ciliary dysfunction is a major mechanism underlying SCA11 pathology.
evaluation: Claims C11, C112, C122, C146, and C147 represent the main conclusions inferred from the collective experimental data. The convergence of Ttbk2 and Ift88 phenotypes, cell-autonomous PC effects, temporal progression from cilia loss to synaptic degeneration to PC death, and recapitulation of SCA11 features provide strong support for this conclusion.

result: The ciliary phenotypes differ between Ttbk2 and Ift88 conditional mutants: Ttbk2c.mut shows rapid complete cilia loss while Ift88c.mut shows partial loss with shortened cilia and loss of AC3.
evaluation: Claims C123-C126 are supported by comparative data showing nearly complete cilia loss within 20 days in Ttbk2c.mut (Figure 5D,E) versus moderate reduction at 3 months in Ift88c.mut (Figure 6A,C) with shortened cilia (Figure 6D) and AC3 loss (Figure 6G). This differential phenotype is important for mechanistic interpretation.

result: Loss of AC3 from cilia in Ift88c.mut animals may contribute to cerebellar degeneration through disrupted cAMP signaling.
evaluation: Claims C130 and C131 are speculative (C131 is marked as SPECULATION). While AC3 loss is documented (Figure 6G), the causal link to cellular changes is not directly tested. The authors acknowledge this is a candidate mechanism but do not provide functional evidence that AC3 loss specifically drives the phenotype. Additional experiments manipulating AC3 or cAMP would be needed.

result: TTBK2 may play a more central role than IFT machinery in maintaining cilia stability in adult neurons.
evaluation: Claims C136-C139 are partially speculative (C139 marked as SPECULATION). While the differential kinetics of cilia loss between Ttbk2c.mut (rapid, complete) and Ift88c.mut (slow, partial) are documented, the interpretation that TTBK2 is more central to stability is inferred rather than directly tested. Alternative explanations (e.g., incomplete Ift88 knockout, compensatory mechanisms) are not fully excluded.

result: Ttbk2c.mut mice exhibit systemic ciliopathy phenotypes including obesity and cystic kidneys at 4 months of age.
evaluation: Claims C31-C33 are supported by quantitative weight data (32.29±1.86 vs 46.33±2.04 g, p=0.0003, n=7) and H&E staining showing polycystic kidneys (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-F). Western blot confirms TTBK2 loss (Figure 1—figure supplement 2G). These systemic phenotypes are consistent with other global cilia knockout models (C31, Davenport et al., 2007).

result: Control animals show no phenotypic differences from pre-induction Ttbk2fl/fl;Ubc-Cre-ERT2+ animals at P21.
evaluation: Claim C30 is supported by data showing no differences in cilia abundance, molecular layer thickness, or VGLUT2 puncta across control genotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C). This validates the experimental design and confirms that the Cre transgene alone does not cause phenotypes.

result: TTBK2 may have additional roles beyond ciliogenesis that contribute to neurodegeneration, potentially including signal relay from cilium to cell body.
evaluation: Claims C144 and C145 are explicitly speculative. While the authors cite evidence for TTBK2 functions in microtubule regulation (C141-C142) and synaptic vesicle trafficking (C143), they acknowledge they cannot exclude non-ciliary contributions to the phenotype. The convergence with Ift88 phenotypes argues against this, but it remains untested.

result: Cilia may play broader roles in maintaining neuronal connectivity and viability in the brain, with implications for ciliopathy patients as they age.
evaluation: Claims C148-C150 are explicitly speculative extrapolations from the current findings. While the data support a role for cilia in PC maintenance, extension to other neuron types and prediction of clinical outcomes in ciliopathy patients are not directly tested. These represent important hypotheses for future work rather than supported conclusions.
